topic.title: Transformer Architecture, Optimization, and Learnability
topic.overview: This topic studies why particular Transformer designs train efficiently and which functions their learning dynamics favor. Architectural search, initialization, nonlinear attention, positional mechanisms, and sparse circuits all affect the gap between representing a function in principle and learning it from data. Capacity alone does not determine which solutions optimization will find.
topic.whyItMatters: Understanding that gap can guide cheaper architectures and explain failures that simply increasing size does not resolve. A modification should be judged through both compute use and the tasks or distributions it enables.
topic.evolution: Representatives include evolutionary architecture search in 2019, improved initialization, and primitive-level efficiency search in 2021. Later theory studies nonlinear in-context learning and pruning. A 2026 parameter-volume analysis examines why sensitive Boolean functions can occupy difficult-to-reach regions despite being expressible. These threads connect design experiments with increasingly specific explanations of training bias.
openQuestions: Which architectural changes improve learnability rather than only expressivity?
How far do tractable in-context-learning analyses predict behavior in full pretrained systems?

papers.tldr: Controlled experiments show that recurrent Transformers can allocate compute according to difficulty without learning to generalize to larger unseen problems.

papers.title: Understanding the Parameter Space Volume of Transformers Encoding Boolean Functions
papers.tldr: The paper links Transformers' difficulty learning sensitive Boolean functions to the vanishing parameter-space volume occupied by those functions.

papers.title: Weight-sparse transformers have interpretable circuits
papers.tldr: Training transformers with sparse weights produces unusually readable task circuits, with a measured trade-off between interpretability and capability.

papers.title: Why Are Linear RNNs More Parallelizable?
papers.tldr: Complexity-theoretic connections explain linear RNNs' parallel efficiency and distinguish the expressive power of recurrent architectures.
